title: Multilayer Virtualized Systems Analysis with Kernel Tracing

publication.venue: IEEE Future Internet of Things and Cloud Workshops (FiCloudW)

abstract_source: No public abstract captured in the current local catalog; summary limited to verified bibliographic metadata and the paper title.
description: The paper fuses synchronized host and virtual-machine kernel traces into a Fused Virtual Machine view that exposes how VM threads, virtual CPUs, hypervisor transitions, and physical CPUs interact.

summary.core_contribution: The paper fuses synchronized host and virtual-machine kernel traces into a Fused Virtual Machine view that exposes how VM threads, virtual CPUs, hypervisor transitions, and physical CPUs interact.
summary.problem: Virtual-machine boundaries obscure direct and indirect interactions between guest activity, hypervisor transitions, and host scheduling or I/O. A process can appear uninterrupted inside a guest while being preempted or delayed on the host.
summary.method: Collect synchronized LTTng kernel traces from hosts and VMs, align them using hypercalls and incremental convex-hull synchronization, and fuse them into a state-history representation. The Fused Virtual Machine view maps guest vCPUs onto physical CPUs and exposes cross-layer state.
summary.findings: In the three-VM use cases, the fused view reveals host preemption, process migration, vmentry/vmexit transitions, and physical I/O handling that are invisible or ambiguous in a VM-only view.
summary.limitations: Evaluation is qualitative and use-case based. Containers are explicitly outside scope. The inspected paper does not report hardware, OS/kernel versions, trace volumes, run counts, timing results, or quantitative detection accuracy.
summary.future_work: Reuse existing analysis tools, parallelize fused analysis, and extend the approach to Java, Python, containers, and interactions among VMs on different nodes, as stated in the conclusion.
